items.answer: Augmented reality on the reality-virtuality continuum is the intermediate state in which the real environment is augmented with virtual content.

Mixed reality, in a broad sense, is the entire space between the real environment extreme and the virtual environment extreme of the reality-virtuality continuum, containing different degrees of augmentation of the real environment with virtual content and of the virtual environment with real content.
The reality-virtuality continuum is a scale whose extremes are a completely real environment with nothing virtual and a completely virtual environment with nothing real.

Virtual reality (VR) is, according to the Miriam Webster dictionary, an artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli, in which sights and sounds play a primary role and are provided by a computer, possibly along with other sensory stimuli, and in which a person's actions partially determine what happens in the environment.

questions.question: According to the Merriam-Webster definition, what is augmented reality?
options: An enhanced version of reality that overlays digital information on an image of something being viewed
An artificial environment experienced through sensory stimuli
The entire space between a completely real and a completely virtual environment
A medium consisting of immersive computer-generated environments
questions.explanation: The dictionary definition describes augmented reality as an enhanced version of reality created by technology, primarily computer technology, to overlay digital information on an image of something being viewed through a device.

questions.question: According to the systemic definition of augmented reality, what must happen when a user interacts with digital content added to the real-world view?
options: The interaction must be performed on a separate interface
The interaction is reflected immediately in real time
The interaction is reflected only after the interaction ends
The interaction must replace the real-world view
questions.explanation: The systemic definition states that an AR system is interactive in real time, so interaction with the digital content added to the real-world view is reflected immediately.

questions.question: According to the four-characteristic account of augmented reality, how must the digital enhancement be experienced?
options: Through a separate interface from the environment
Through a static display with no real-world view
Through the user's sensory organs
Through a completely virtual environment
questions.explanation: One of the four AR characteristics is that the enhancement is experienced through the user's sensory organs.

questions.question: What conclusion follows if a system does not satisfy one of the four characteristics of augmented reality?
options: It is automatically a mixed reality system
It is automatically a virtual reality system
It is not an augmented reality system
It can still be called an augmented reality system
questions.explanation: A system is identified as an AR system by checking the four AR characteristics one by one, and it is an AR system only if all four are satisfied; if at least one is not satisfied, it is not an AR system.

data.text: Augmented reality is an enhanced version of reality created by overlaying digital information on a real-world view. An AR system enhances the real world with digital content that is registered in 3D, experienced through the senses, and allows for interaction with that content. A system is only classified as augmented reality if all four of these characteristics are satisfied.
points: Augmented reality is an enhanced version of reality created by overlaying digital information on a real-world view.
An AR system enhances the real world with digital content, registers it in 3D, provides a sensory experience, and supports interaction with that content.
A system is only identified as an augmented reality system if all four of these characteristics are satisfied.

questions.question: How do augmented reality and virtual reality differ in their effect on the user's experience of reality?
options: AR and VR both completely replace the user's real-world perception with a virtual environment.
AR alters the ongoing perception of the real world, while VR completely replaces it with a virtual environment.
VR alters the ongoing perception of the real world, while AR completely replaces it with a virtual environment.
AR and VR both only alter the ongoing perception of the real world.
questions.explanation: AR alters the ongoing perception of the real world, whereas VR completely replaces the user's sense of reality with a virtual environment.

questions.question: Why can a VR system present an object or place that does not physically exist?
options: Because it superimposes non-existent digital content over a real-world view.
Because it requires the experienced place to exist and then enhances it with digital content.
Because it only alters the ongoing perception of a physically real room.
Because it creates a virtual environment instead of requiring the experienced place to exist.
questions.explanation: A VR system does not require the physical existence of an object or place because it creates a virtual environment.

questions.question: How can an AR system display digital content in a view of a real room?
options: It can remove the real-world view and present a separate virtual scene.
It can show furniture only if that furniture physically exists in the room.
It can replace the room with a virtual environment so the real room is no longer visible.
It can superimpose non-existent furniture as digital content over the real-world view of the room.
questions.explanation: An AR system can superimpose extra information, such as non-existent furniture, as digital content over the real-world view of a room.

data.text: AR alters the perception of the real world, while VR replaces it with a virtual environment. VR systems do not require a physical place to exist, but AR and MR systems require the place being experienced to exist. AR can superimpose extra information, such as digital content, over a real-world view.
points: AR alters the perception of the real world, while VR replaces it with a virtual environment.
VR systems do not require a physical place to exist, but AR and MR systems require the place to exist.
AR can superimpose digital content over a real-world view.

questions.question: What is the state of agreement on a precise definition of mixed reality?
options: Practitioners and the literature agree on one precise definition.
A single developer-oriented definition is universally adopted.
Only the dictionary definition is accepted by all practitioners.
There is no agreement among practitioners and the literature.
questions.explanation: The segment states that practitioners and the literature do not agree on the precise definition of mixed reality.

questions.question: What limitation does the dictionary definition of mixed reality have?
options: It does not mention any combination of physical and virtual elements.
It excludes interaction with digital content in the view of reality.
It treats mixed reality as completely replacing the real world.
It is not categorical about how mixed reality differs from VR or AR.
questions.explanation: The dictionary definition combines physical and virtual elements but does not clearly state how MR differs from VR or AR.

questions.question: According to one definition, how is augmented reality related to mixed reality?
options: AR is included in MR, which spans everything between the real and virtual extremes.
AR is an extreme separate from the MR range.
MR is only the virtual extreme and excludes AR.
AR replaces MR as the broader category.
questions.explanation: One definition places MR as everything in between the real and virtual extremes, so AR is included in that broader MR.

questions.question: From a developer's point of view, what can make an application mixed reality in one definition?
options: Combining AR and VR technologies in the same application or on the same device.
Requiring the place being experienced to exist physically.
Creating a fully immersive environment without any physical reference.
Overlaying digital content on a view of reality and allowing interaction with it.
questions.explanation: One definition treats an application as MR when it combines AR and VR technologies in the same application or device.

questions.question: Why may mixed reality be used as a synonym for augmented reality by many people?
options: Because both combine augmented and virtual reality technologies in one device.
Because both describe every point between the real and virtual extremes.
Because both let users see reality enhanced with overlaid digital content and interact with it.
Because both replace the user's view of reality with a virtual environment.
questions.explanation: In many people's usage, MR is a synonym for AR because both involve viewing reality augmented with digital content and interacting with that content.

data.text: There is no consensus on the precise definition of mixed reality (MR), with various definitions describing it as a range between real and virtual environments, a combination of AR and VR technologies, or a more capable version of AR. Because many people use mixed reality synonymously with augmented reality, this course treats the two terms as interchangeable.
points: There is no agreement on the precise definition of mixed reality (MR).
Definitions of MR vary, ranging from a continuum between real and virtual environments to a combination of AR and VR technologies or a more capable version of AR.
Mixed reality is often used as a synonym for augmented reality (AR).
This course treats mixed reality and augmented reality as the same technology.

questions.question: How does the course treat the terms mixed reality and augmented reality?
options: It treats augmented reality as a subset of mixed reality.
It treats mixed reality as a combination of augmented reality and virtual reality.
It treats mixed reality as a subset of augmented reality.
It treats them as interchangeable terms for the same technology.
questions.explanation: The course assumes mixed reality is the same technology and idea as augmented reality and uses that assumption to keep the later discussion simple.

data.text: In this course, mixed reality is assumed to be the same technology and idea as augmented reality for simplicity in subsequent discussions.
points: Mixed reality is treated as the same technology as augmented reality in this course.

questions.question: How do augmented reality and virtual reality differ in their relationship to the physical environment being experienced?
questions.reference_answer: Augmented reality alters the ongoing perception of the real world, whereas virtual reality completely replaces the user's sense of reality with a virtual environment. A virtual reality system does not require the physical existence of an object or place, because it creates a virtual environment, whereas an augmented reality system requires the place being experienced to exist.

questions.question: Why is it not enough for a system to overlay digital content on a real-world view in order to be an augmented reality system?
questions.reference_answer: The dictionary definition describes augmented reality as overlaying digital information on an image of something viewed through a device. The systemic definition requires an augmented reality system to combine the real world with virtual content, be interactive in real time, and be registered in 3D. The four-characteristic identification test requires the enhancement to be registered in 3D, experienced through sensory organs, and supported by interaction in the enhanced environment, and a system is an augmented reality system only if all four characteristics are satisfied.

questions.question: How do definitions of mixed reality relate to augmented reality and the reality-virtuality continuum, and why does the course use mixed reality and augmented reality interchangeably?
questions.reference_answer: There is no agreement on a precise definition of mixed reality. In a broad sense, mixed reality is the entire space between the real environment extreme and the virtual environment extreme of the reality-virtuality continuum, and one definition says it comprises everything in between those extremes, so augmented reality is included. Another definition treats mixed reality as a synonym for augmented reality. Because the definitions are confusing, the course assumes mixed reality is the same technology and idea as augmented reality and treats the terms as interchangeable.
